title: Health-management algorithm racial-bias study
system_purpose: Identify patients for high-risk care-management support
affected_groups: Black patients; White patients; care-management teams
verified_facts: The peer-reviewed study found that an algorithm using health-care cost as a proxy for health needs produced racial bias at a given risk score.
reported_harm: Black patients were less likely to receive additional help despite being sicker at the same score; the harm is inequitable allocation of care-management resources.
quantitative_evidence: The study estimated changing the target would increase Black patients receiving additional help from 17.7% to 46.5%.
limitations: The publication does not evaluate a chat interface, Vietnam population, or a symptom-routing model.

title: External validation of Epic Sepsis Model
system_purpose: Predict sepsis risk for inpatient clinical workflow
decision_impact: Clinical alerting and potential timing of antibiotic response
verified_facts: The external-validation study evaluated a proprietary model implemented at hundreds of hospitals and reported that, at its selected threshold, 183 of 2,552 sepsis hospitalizations had a qualifying score but no timely antibiotics.
reported_harm: Missed or poorly calibrated alerts can contribute to delayed recognition, while excessive or unhelpful alerts can burden clinicians; the study does not prove causation for each outcome.
quantitative_evidence: At score 6 or higher, 183 of 2,552 sepsis hospitalizations were identified before or within three hours after sepsis without timely antibiotics; the paper also reports 1709 missed sepsis hospitalizations.
limitations: The evaluation is an inpatient predictive model at one academic medical center, not a causal study of treatment outcomes or a consumer symptom-routing chatbot.

title: NEDA Tessa eating-disorder chatbot suspension
system_purpose: Provide information and support related to eating disorders
affected_groups: People seeking eating-disorder support; advocates; care providers
verified_facts: NPR reported user screenshots of Tessa providing dieting or weight-management guidance and reported that NEDA suspended the chatbot after content received by some testers may have been harmful and unrelated to the programme.
reported_harm: Users and advocates reported that dieting or weight-management guidance could worsen distress or reinforce harmful behaviour in people seeking eating-disorder support; this is a reported harm, not a clinically measured rate.
quantitative_evidence: NPR's report provides qualitative incident reporting and screenshots, not a denominator, validated harm rate, or controlled comparison.
limitations: The article reports accounts from users, NEDA, and the vendor; it does not independently establish the exact technical mechanism, prevalence, clinical causality, or performance of all health chatbots.
